applicability_evaluation.model_entry_selection: Entry selection is evaluated separately from corpus construction; the application records its workflow per run.

provenance.graph: Derived from ten fictional diagnostic guides and an explicit vehicle-variant source schedule.
provenance.oracle: Reviewer-authored source-linked paths, not model-scored ground truth.

review.verdict: Historical v4.1.1 only: conditionally fit after four blocking findings were corrected. Not a review of the expanded corpus.
review.scope: Historical v4.1.1 review only: three original families and vehicle variants. The seven new v4.2.0 families have not received this model review.
review.change_policy: Freeze sources and artifact hashes. Model failures alone do not justify changing evidence or expected outcomes.

prior_versions.correction: New procedures inherited a Model A safety notice. The final notice names each actual applicable vehicle; no diagnostic source, public input, branch rule or expected path changed.

input_revision.reason: User-requested diagnostic variety, not a response to model accuracy.
input_revision.changes: Seven independently authored fictional problem families; repeated applicability cases move into the evaluation picker.
input_revision.unchanged: All 87 historical public inputs, source rules, graph nodes/edges and expected paths; only their demo presentation flag changes.

comparison_compatibility: v4.2.0 adds entry candidates and new authored families. Historical accuracy/timing results are not comparable and do not establish performance on this expanded graph.
limitations: All Brand X vehicles, procedures and reference values in this dataset are fictional; review supplied records only, not real vehicle work.
Ten fictional vehicles and thirty-seven procedures; not manufacturer or expert-validated guidance.

Thirty procedures are correlated variants of three families; seven additional families each have one explicitly applicable vehicle. There are ten diagnostic families, not thirty-seven independent ones.
Matched vehicle cases are authored counterfactuals, not independent real workshop jobs or a held-out accuracy benchmark.
Numeric limits and controlled comparison criteria are invented.
INDICATES is supported by the schema but not invented where the sources do not need it.
